title: Anchored billing ladders for asymmetric I/O and streaming
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Run a controlled experiment and analysis to evaluate an anchored billing ladder that separates input vs output token rates, applies a per-request streaming floor, and tests an anchored minimum charge tier for low-volume enterprise customers.

Goals: (1) Measure revenue and usage elasticity when charging asymmetric input/output token rates; (2) Validate whether a streaming floor reduces tail latency cost while preserving developer adoption; (3) Determine appropriate anchor tiers (minimum monthly commitments) for enterprise contracts to improve revenue predictability without blocking self-serve growth.

Scope: Design experiment variants for hosted API only (not Dedicated/Private). Metrics tracked: effective $/net-token, conversion/drop-off rates during onboarding, LTV projection uplift, average per-request latency, billing disputes incidence, and support volume related to confusion about streaming floors.

Key stakeholders: PM (Ava), Pricing lead (Samir), Revenue Ops, Legal (contracts), Billing engineering, SDK leads, Analytics (A/B platform).
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix defined with at least 3 variants: baseline, asymmetric IO (0.6x input / 1.4x output), and anchored-minimum with streaming floor
Billing and meter changes validated in staging with simulated traffic
A/B rollout plan approved with statistical power calc showing >80% power for conversion and revenue uplift metrics
Contract language draft for enterprise anchor tiers produced and reviewed by Legal
Dashboard captures: per-variant ARPU, churn signals, dispute rate, and latency-cost tradeoff
